# CRW-895 after the pre-merge evaluation of 3d1fe314: the shapes of its defects d1..d7 and their neighbours.
# ../repo is the managed checkout itself, .. is the slot root. Format: see shellwrite_repro_test.go.

=== CRW-895-f1 | R
--why A test that matches every entry and the root guards nothing (the pre-merge evaluation, d1).
find ../repo -name '*' -delete

=== CRW-895-f2 | R
--why -path '*' matches the root as well.
find ../repo -path '*' -delete

=== CRW-895-f3 | R
--why -regex '.*' matches the root as well.
find ../repo -regex '.*' -delete

=== CRW-895-f4 | R
--why -name '????' matches the four letters of repo, the root's own name.
find ../repo -name '????' -delete

=== CRW-895-f5 | R
--why From inside the checkout a match-all test is the same as no test.
find . -name '*' -delete

=== CRW-895-f6 | B
--why -type f keeps the action to files, so the root stays whatever -name matches.
find ../repo -name '*' -type f -delete

=== CRW-895-f7 | R
--why -name 'r*' matches repo, the root, which find names by its spelling in the start point.
find ../repo -name 'r*' -delete

=== CRW-895-f8 | R
--why A negated test that does not match the root's name matches the root.
find ../repo ! -name x -delete

=== CRW-895-f9 | B
--why A negated test whose pattern matches the root's name leaves the root out.
find ../repo ! -name repo -delete

=== CRW-895-f10 | B
--why From '.', find matches -name against '.', which r* does not match: the issue control.
find . -name 'r*' -delete

=== CRW-895-f11 | R
--why -iname matches the root's name without case.
find ../repo -iname 'REPO' -delete

=== CRW-895-f12 | B
--why -type f: the issue control spelled with a start that names the checkout.
find ../repo -type f -delete

=== CRW-895-f13 | R
--why The alternative of a group that tests nothing the root fails reaches -delete.
find ../repo \( -name x -o -name '*' \) -delete

=== CRW-895-g1 | R
--why find -files0-from reads the start points from a file at run time; they can be the slot or an ancestor (evaluation d2).
find -files0-from roots.list -type f -delete

=== CRW-895-g2 | R
--why The start points read from standard input are not known either.
find -files0-from - -name x -delete

=== CRW-895-g3 | R
--why The same with -exec rm.
find -files0-from roots.list -name x -exec rm {} +

=== CRW-895-g4 | R
--why find -files0-from as the producer of xargs prints names the reader cannot see.
find -files0-from roots.list | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-h1 | R
--why printf prints ../repo from %s: the format and the argument are joined before xargs reads them (evaluation d3).
printf '../%s\n' repo | xargs git worktree remove --force

=== CRW-895-h2 | R
--why printf turns the octal escape \160 into p: the output names ../repo.
printf '../re\160o\n' | xargs git worktree remove --force

=== CRW-895-h3 | R
--why Two arguments of %s/%s join into the checkout's path.
printf '%s/%s\n' .. repo | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-h4 | R
--why %b decodes \x70 in its argument.
printf '%b' '../re\x70o' | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-h5 | R
--why echo -e decodes \x70.
echo -e '../re\x70o' | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-h6 | R
--why xargs removes the backslash from .\./repo: it reads ../repo.
echo '.\./repo' | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-h7 | R
--why xargs removes the quotes around a name.
printf "'../repo'\n" | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-h8 | B
--why A printed name inside the checkout.
printf '%s\n' build/old.o | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-h9 | B
--why A printed name that is a sibling of the checkout.
printf '../%s\n' other | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-h10 | R
--why One of two printed names is the checkout.
printf '%s\n' ../other ../repo | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-h11 | R
--why %s with no separator joins its arguments: .. and /repo make ../repo.
printf '%s' .. /repo | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-h12 | R
--why A backslash in echo without -e is literal in bash and an escape in dash; the reader judges both.
echo '..\x2frepo' | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-i1 | R
--why xargs -I{} puts the printed name into the template: ../{} with repo is ../repo (evaluation d4).
echo repo | xargs -I{} git worktree remove --force '../{}'

=== CRW-895-i2 | R
--why -I{} with rmdir.
echo repo | xargs -I{} rmdir ../{}

=== CRW-895-i3 | R
--why -i is -I{}.
echo repo | xargs -i rmdir ../{}

=== CRW-895-i4 | R
--why -I@ names the replace string; a non-recursive rm of the checkout is refused too.
echo repo | xargs -I@ rm ../@

=== CRW-895-i5 | R
--why The replace string may stand for a word of the command itself.
echo worktree | xargs -I{} git {} remove ../repo

=== CRW-895-i6 | R
--why The replace string stands for the program: the reader reads rm -rf ../repo.
echo rm | xargs -I{} {} -rf ../repo

=== CRW-895-i7 | R
--why A source the text does not name, with a replace string in the operand, may produce any name.
ls | xargs -I{} rm ../{}

=== CRW-895-i8 | B
--why A whole-word replace string for a program whose list the text does not name: the control.
ls | xargs -I{} rm {}

=== CRW-895-i9 | B
--why The replace string inside the checkout.
echo old.o | xargs -I{} rm build/{}

=== CRW-895-i10 | B
--why rmdir of a directory inside the checkout.
echo build | xargs -I{} rmdir {}

=== CRW-895-i11 | R
--why xargs -d : splits the input at the colon.
printf 'a:../repo' | xargs -d : rmdir

=== CRW-895-i12 | R
--why xargs -0 reads the whole input as one name.
printf '../repo' | xargs -0 rmdir

=== CRW-895-i13 | R
--why xargs -d '\n'.
printf '../repo\n' | xargs -d '\n' rmdir

=== CRW-895-i14 | R
--why The replace string inside the text of a shell the template runs.
echo repo | xargs -I{} sh -c 'rmdir ../{}'

=== CRW-895-i15 | R
--why A source that is not read, with the replace string inside a shell text.
ls | xargs -I{} sh -c 'rmdir ../{}'

=== CRW-895-j1 | R
--why head -c cuts the printed name down to ../repo (evaluation d5).
printf '../repoX' | head -c 7 | xargs git worktree remove --force

=== CRW-895-j2 | R
--why tail -c keeps the last bytes.
printf 'x../repo' | tail -c 7 | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-j3 | R
--why grep -o prints only the match.
echo '../repoX' | grep -o '../repo' | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-j4 | B
--why head -n keeps a whole line of a list that does not name the checkout.
echo ../other | head -n 1 | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-j5 | R
--why head -n keeps whole lines: the line names the checkout.
echo ../repo | head -n 1 | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-j6 | R
--why sort -u keeps the lines.
echo ../repo | sort -u | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-j7 | R
--why grep -v keeps the lines that do not match.
echo ../repo | grep -v x | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-j8 | R
--why tail -n 1 keeps the last line, which names the checkout.
printf 'a\n../repo\n' | tail -n 1 | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-j9 | R
--why A backslash-newline joins lines for xargs; tail leaves the checkout's line alone.
printf 'X\\\n../repo' | tail -n 1 | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-j10 | R
--why cut rewrites the list.
echo '../repoX' | cut -c1-7 | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-j11 | R
--why pwd prints the directory the command runs in, which is the checkout.
pwd | xargs git worktree remove

=== CRW-895-j12 | R
--why realpath prints the absolute path of its operand.
realpath . | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-j13 | R
--why git rev-parse --show-toplevel prints the checkout.
git rev-parse --show-toplevel | xargs git worktree remove

=== CRW-895-j14 | R
--why ls -d prints its operands as they are.
ls -d .. | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-j15 | R
--why An absolute program path is the same program.
/bin/echo ../repo | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-j16 | B
--why ls names nothing in the text: the issue control.
ls build | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-k1 | B
--why Every action is reached only for a regular file, parentheses or not (evaluation d6).
find . -type f \( -exec rm {} + \)

=== CRW-895-k2 | B
--why The test stands in the group.
find . \( -type f -exec rm {} + \)

=== CRW-895-k3 | R
--why A group with no test around the action.
find . \( -exec rm {} + \)

=== CRW-895-k4 | B
--why A test before a group whose alternatives test nothing themselves.
find ../repo -type f \( -name x -o -true \) -delete

=== CRW-895-k5 | B
--why A group of tests before the action: the issue control.
find . \( -type f -o -type l \) -exec rm {} +

=== CRW-895-l1 | B
--why The shell text ignores the names xargs hands it (evaluation d7).
echo ../repo | xargs sh -c 'rm build/old.o'

=== CRW-895-l2 | R
--why The shell text removes what xargs hands it as its arguments.
echo ../repo | xargs sh -c 'rm "$@"' _

=== CRW-895-l3 | B
--why find -exec sh -c with a fixed removal does not use the placeholder.
find ../repo -exec sh -c 'rm build/old.o' \;

=== CRW-895-l4 | R
--why find -exec bash -c removes the placeholder, which is the checkout.
find ../repo -exec bash -c 'rm "$0"' {} \;

=== CRW-895-l5 | B
--why A fixed removal in a nested shell under find from the checkout.
find . -exec sh -c 'rm build/old.o' \;
